title: Bidirectional token floors with enterprise SQ alignment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Run a controlled experiment that applies asymmetric ingress (input) and egress (output) token floors and graduated discounts, while simultaneously updating enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) responses and contract language templates to reflect directional billing mechanics. Goal is to validate revenue-neutral pricing levers that better align unit economics with our serving cost profile (output-heavy models cost more) and to ensure legal/sales collateral accurately represents those mechanics for enterprise deals.
experiment_hypothesis: If we introduce a modest output-weighted floor and a lower input floor plus gradual output discount at higher volumes, then average gross margin will improve on text-generation workloads without materially increasing churn; enterprise legal and SQ updates will reduce negotiation time for affected deals by making token floor mechanics explicit.
metric_definitions: Primary: gross margin per request (USD/token-adjusted) and net MRR delta for pilot customers. Secondary: churn delta at 30/60 days, negotiation time (days) for enterprise deals that reference SQ, billing disputes count. Success targets: >= 3% improvement in per-token gross margin, <= 1% increase in churn, >= 20% reduction in average negotiation time for pilot enterprise contracts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Billing pipeline emits separate ingress and egress lines in invoices for pilot customers; 2) Analytics dashboard shows directional token usage and margin; 3) Legal has updated SQ language and contract clause (v1) and sales trainings completed; 4) Pilot cohort results meet success targets or provide actionable rollback plan.
roll_out_plan: Phase 0 (Technical prep, 2 weeks): Billing schemas, reporting, analytics signal. Phase 1 (Pilot, 6 weeks): 8 existing enterprise customers opt-in; 4 mid-market self-serve accounts included for contrast. Phase 2 (Analysis, 2 weeks): evaluate metrics, gather sales/legal feedback. Phase 3 (Decision): scale or rollback and prepare customer communications.
data_sources: billing DB (per-token logs), Console cost-per-token traces, signups/usage from product analytics, contract negotiation logs in Salesforce, security questionnaire responses repository (internal Confluence/Drive folder), sample invoices.
stakeholders: Product: Miguel Santos (owner), Revenue Ops: Laila Chen, Legal: Priya Nair, Sales: Ethan Morales, Engineering: Karthik Rao, Finance: Jenna Park, DevRel: Samira Ortiz
notes: Trade-offs discussed: complexity on invoices vs customer clarity; engineering estimated +2 sprint overhead to support split ingress/egress metering. Finance prefers conservative floors to avoid negative churn impact. Legal requested explicit examples in SQ to avoid ambiguity. Sales asked for grace period and one-time migration credits for affected customers.
review_feedback: - Legal (Priya): add clause that clarifies streaming partial tokens rounding behavior; - Finance (Jenna): simulate top-20 customers under proposal before pilot; - Eng (Karthik): implement feature flag and telemetry to avoid broad rollout; - Sales (Ethan): request FAQ and comparison table for AE enablement.
